tasks.entryName: Riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields (Weil theorem)
tasks.entryDescription: Jacobian/endomorphism eigenvalues; intersection theory on C×C; Stepanov–Bombieri polynomial method; Deligne's general Weil-conjectures route.
tasks.currentSketch: For a smooth projective curve over F_q, Frobenius acts on H¹ of its Jacobian/étale cohomology; the zeta numerator is its characteristic polynomial. Weil’s positivity/intersection pairing implies every eigenvalue has absolute value √q. Intersection-theoretic proof encodes Frobenius and diagonal as divisors on C×C and applies a positivity inequality. Deligne generalizes cohomologically to higher dimension; Stepanov gives an elementary polynomial auxiliary-function bound.

existingReferences.label: Weil, Numbers of solutions of equations in finite fields
existingReferences.locator: Weil’s original proof of RH for curves; separate modern methods require their own sources

tasks.entryName: Jones polynomial is an invariant of links
tasks.entryDescription: Reidemeister-move skein relation; Temperley–Lieb algebras; quantum-group representations; Chern–Simons/topological quantum field theory. State the exact normalization and link equivalence.
tasks.currentSketch: Define the bracket recursively by ⟨L⟩=A⟨L₀⟩+A⁻¹⟨L∞⟩ and ⟨L⊔○⟩=−(A²+A⁻²)⟨L⟩. Check the three Reidemeister moves: II and III preserve the bracket, while I multiplies by a writhe-dependent factor. Normalize by (−A³)^{−w(L)} to obtain an ambient-isotopy invariant (then change variables for Jones V).

existingReferences.label: Kauffman, State models and the Jones polynomial
existingReferences.locator: State-sum construction/invariance under Reidemeister moves

tasks.entryDescription: Reidemeister-move skein relation; Temperley–Lieb algebras; quantum-group representations; Chern–Simons/topological quantum field theory. State the exact normalization and link equivalence.
tasks.currentSketch: Represent braid generators by Temperley–Lieb operators e_i with e_i²=δe_i and e_ie_{i±1}e_i=e_i. The Markov trace is invariant under braid conjugation and stabilization after a writhe normalization; Alexander’s theorem plus Markov’s theorem then makes the resulting closure polynomial a link invariant.

tasks.entryDescription: Reidemeister-move skein relation; Temperley–Lieb algebras; quantum-group representations; Chern–Simons/topological quantum field theory. State the exact normalization and link equivalence.
tasks.currentSketch: A ribbon/quasitriangular quantum-group representation assigns operators to crossings via the R-matrix and evaluation/coevaluation to cups and caps. Yang–Baxter ensures Reidemeister III, invertibility handles II, and twist correction handles I; choosing the fundamental U_q(sl₂) representation yields the Jones polynomial up to normalization.

tasks.entryName: Constant-curvature manifolds are locally modeled on spherical, Euclidean, or hyperbolic space
tasks.entryDescription: Jacobi-field comparison and exponential coordinates; Frobenius/integrability of parallel frames; Cartan connection/structure equations.
tasks.currentSketch: In a sufficiently small normal neighborhood, Jacobi fields along radial geodesics satisfy J″+R(J,γ′)γ′=0. Constant sectional curvature makes this scalar equation identical to that in the model sphere/Euclidean/hyperbolic space; matching initial data makes exponential-coordinate metrics locally isometric. Parallel-frame/Cartan proofs integrate the same structure equations.

existingReferences.label: Lee, Riemannian Manifolds: An Introduction to Curvature
existingReferences.locator: Chapter on constant sectional curvature and local space-form theorem

tasks.entryName: Hodge theorem (de Rham cohomology represented by harmonic forms)
tasks.entryDescription: Elliptic PDE and Green operators; Hilbert-space orthogonal decomposition; heat-flow convergence to harmonic representatives.
tasks.currentSketch: On a compact Riemannian manifold, ellipticity gives Green operator G on the orthogonal complement of harmonic forms and ΔG=GΔ=I−H. For closed α, α=Hα+dδGα, so its class has harmonic representative; if harmonic α is exact, ⟨α,α⟩=⟨α,dβ⟩=⟨δα,β⟩=0, proving uniqueness.

existingReferences.label: Jost, Riemannian Geometry and Geometric Analysis
existingReferences.locator: Hodge theory chapter: elliptic theory, orthogonal decomposition, harmonic representatives

tasks.entryName: Borsuk–Ulam theorem
tasks.entryDescription: Degree/mod-2 homology; Tucker's lemma and combinatorial antipodal labeling; equivariant topology.
tasks.currentSketch: If f:S^n→R^n had f(x)≠f(−x) everywhere, then g(x)=(f(x)−f(−x))/||…|| would be an odd map S^n→S^{n−1}. Its restriction/quotient contradicts the mod-2 cohomology or degree computation for antipodal maps. Tucker’s lemma gives a combinatorial obstruction to such an odd labeling; equivariant-index proofs package the same obstruction.

existingReferences.label: Matoušek, Using the Borsuk–Ulam Theorem
existingReferences.locator: Chapter 1, degree/mod-2 and combinatorial Tucker proof

tasks.entryName: Noether's theorem (continuous symmetry yields a conserved quantity)
tasks.entryDescription: Euler–Lagrange variational identity; Hamiltonian/symplectic moment-map formulation; current conservation via differential forms. Specify the finite-dimensional or field-theoretic version.
tasks.currentSketch: For a one-parameter variational symmetry with infinitesimal generator η and Lagrangian L, differentiate the invariance identity at the identity and use Euler–Lagrange equations: d/dt(∂L/∂q̇·η−B)=0. Hamiltonian moment-map and differential-form currents are corresponding formulations. Field-theoretic versions require boundary terms and regularity assumptions.

existingReferences.label: Olver, Applications of Lie Groups to Differential Equations
existingReferences.locator: Chapter 4, Noether theorem for variational problems; exact finite-dimensional hypotheses
